purpose: Define the complete, compilable shape and observable contract of MonoklError — monokl's single unified error enum — and its Result<T> alias, so a developer (or an AI coding agent parsing variants/fields/Display-text at runtime to decide remediation) never has to guess what a given failure means or ask a clarifying question. Remediation-deciding is scoped explicitly to variant/field discrimination plus exact Display-text matching (AC-001 through AC-021) — it does NOT mean a richer miette::Diagnostic surface (codes/help/url), which this track leaves deliberately inert (AC-002B). This spec also resolves, with stated rationale, two low-risk textual-accuracy gaps between the existing draft and its own downstream call sites: a Display message naming a nonexistent CLI command (AC-020), and an undercounted, miscategorized enumeration of the Json variant's real call sites with a Display string that misdescribes half of them (AC-011). It deliberately does NOT resolve the cache.json corruption-vs-staleness recovery policy question — see non_goals.
scope: The MonoklError enum verbatim (all 14 variants, their field shapes, and their #[error(...)] Display messages, with StaleDiskCache's and Json's messages corrected for accuracy), its derives (thiserror::Error, #[non_exhaustive], the optional miette::Diagnostic behind the "miette" feature) and the crate-wide Result<T> alias. It documents — without resolving — the calling contract gap between persist::init (which intercepts StaleDiskCache only) and persist::flush's fallback path (which intercepts nothing). It does not specify persist.rs's or output.rs's full implementation; those remain separate tracks that must conform to the contract stated here.
non_goals: core-types.md's types (SymbolEntry, Visibility, etc.) — separate track.
The two-contradictory-error-output-mechanisms gap (render_error vs miette, 07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 finding #19) — already a known, separately-tracked gap; not resolved here.

The regex-term hard-fail-vs-silent-drop inconsistency and the NonUtf8Path hard-fail-vs-silent-skip inconsistency (docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 findings #7 and #12 specifically — 07 has four independently-numbered finding sets, each with its own #7/#12; only the Part 1 pair is meant here) — call-site behavioral decisions in query.rs/text_search.rs, not changes to MonoklError's shape.
FileIoError itself (owned by the io-errors crate) — external dependency.
persist.rs's and output.rs's full implementation — not implemented in this track.
PoisonError::into_inner recovery — deliberately not introduced for LockPoisoned; poisoning always propagates as a hard error.

Per-variant miette::Diagnostic metadata (#[diagnostic(code(...), help(...), url(...))], or #[diagnostic(transparent)] bridging Io to FileIoError's own Diagnostic impl) — the derive exists only to satisfy the trait bound today; richer diagnostics are a later track (AC-002B).

The three elided-operation-tag MonoklError::Git construction sites inside git_scope::collect_changes (03-multi-language-platform.md:1428, 1430, 1470) — undetermined by the source as shown; deferred to the git_scope.rs implementation track rather than invented here (AC-015).

persist::flush's fallback load_cache() call receiving the same interception persist::init has for StaleDiskCache — documented as a real, current asymmetry (AC-013B), not fixed, since fixing requires editing persist.rs's verbatim body (01-core-architecture.md §16), out of scope for this error-contract track.

Wiring io_safety::read_to_string_capped into search/inspect/extract/refs/definition — it has zero call sites in the current corpus (AC-016/AC-017), contradicting 03-multi-language-platform.md's own prose per 07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 3 findings #2 and #16. This spec documents the unreachability; making SymlinkRejected/FileTooLarge actually constructible is io_safety.rs implementation work, out of scope here.

MonoklError::TraversalCapExceeded { visited: usize, cap: usize } (docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md §2, line 24) — an adopted-but-not-yet-implemented 15th variant for a future TraitImplIndex/bounded-BFS traversal track. AC-001's 'no 15th variant' claim is scoped to this track's current enum only and does not prohibit this variant; adding it is that future track's job, not this one's.

THE CACHE.JSON CORRUPTION-VS-STALENESS RECOVERY POLICY (whether a MonoklError::Json produced by load_cache's deserialize step should be self-healed the same way StaleDiskCache is, per docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 finding #5 and docs/architecture/error-taxonomy.md's Known contract gaps, gap 1). An earlier draft of this spec attempted to resolve this inside SPEC-001 via judgment_call criteria; two independent review rounds (canon-verifier, canon-auditor) found the resulting criteria kept breaking — asserting an interception that no verbatim code anywhere shows, inventing a brand-new log-message literal with no source grounding, and requiring an implementer to guess whether the self-heal exception also covers persist::flush's fallback path. The auditor's structural diagnosis was correct: this is a genuinely new design decision, not a faithful correction of existing spec text, and per this project's own CLAUDE.md ("superpowers:brainstorming before any design change not already covered by docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md"), it needs a dedicated brainstorming pass before it becomes a spec@1 criterion, not a judgment_call flag riding alongside routine corrections. This is deferred to a follow-on track (working title: SPEC-002, cache-corruption recovery policy), which must go through superpowers:brainstorming first.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: MonoklError (01-core-architecture.md:196-246) has exactly these 14 variants, in this order, with these exact field shapes: Io(#[from] FileIoError) [#[error(transparent)]]; Walk { path: Utf8PathBuf, #[source] source: ignore::Error }; RegexBuild(#[from] grep_regex::Error); NonUtf8Path { path: std::path::PathBuf }; TooManyTerms { count: usize, limit: usize }; TokenizerInit (unit); Json(#[from] serde_json::Error); PathOutsideRoot { path: Utf8PathBuf }; StaleDiskCache (unit); InvalidGitRef { ref_: String, reason: &'static str }; Git { operation: &'static str, message: String }; SymlinkRejected { path: Utf8PathBuf }; FileTooLarge { path: Utf8PathBuf, size: u64, cap: u64 }; LockPoisoned { context: &'static str }. The enum carries exactly these three derive/attribute lines: #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)], #[cfg_attr(feature = "miette", derive(miette::Diagnostic))], #[non_exhaustive]. No 15th variant in this track's enum as of this spec, and no Parse/Query variants (removed per the Post-research correction note at 01-core-architecture.md:251, since nothing in the corpus ever constructs either). This does not prohibit a future, separately-tracked 15th variant: docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md §2 ("Adopted, not yet implemented", line 24) already adopts extending MonoklError with a non-fatal TraversalCapExceeded { visited: usize, cap: usize } variant as part of a TraitImplIndex/bounded-BFS traversal track — that variant is out of scope here (see non_goals), not prohibited by this criterion.

When the crate is built with the "miette" feature enabled, MonoklError additionally derives miette::Diagnostic via #[cfg_attr(feature = "miette", derive(miette::Diagnostic))] (01-core-architecture.md:197). When the feature is disabled, this derive is absent and no miette type appears in MonoklError's public API surface. The "miette" feature is defined as ["dep:miette", "io-errors/miette"] (01-core-architecture.md:87) and is pulled in unconditionally by the "cli" feature (cli = ["dep:clap", "miette"], line 84).

When built with --features miette, for all 14 MonoklError variants (including Io, despite Io wrapping a FileIoError that itself independently derives miette::Diagnostic when io-errors/miette is enabled), <MonoklError as miette::Diagnostic>::code(), ::help(), and ::url() all return None. Zero #[diagnostic(...)] attributes of any kind appear anywhere on the enum. Confirmed by exhaustive grep for '#[diagnostic' across the full docs/spec/*.md corpus and docs/architecture/: zero matches, independently re-confirmed across two review rounds. This is an explicit, intentional, testable boundary of this track: the derive exists solely so downstream code compiles against the Diagnostic trait bound, not to provide a richer diagnostic surface.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The derive's inertness is a fact about the current source (grep-verified twice), but treating that inertness as this track's intentional, permanent-for-now boundary rather than an oversight to fix is a scope judgment. Per-variant diagnostic metadata is deferred to a later track (non_goals).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every function in this spec corpus's Part 1 (01-core-architecture.md) and Part 3 (03-multi-language-platform.md) verbatim code blocks that is pub or pub(crate)-visible within the monokl library crate itself, and whose own signature returns some Result<_, _>, returns exactly crate::error::Result<T> (i.e. std::result::Result<T, MonoklError>) for its own T — with exactly one named exception: git_scope::blob_at_ref_in_repo(repo, git_ref, path) -> std::result::Result<String, String> (03-multi-language-platform.md:1546-1551), a pub(crate) helper whose bare-String error is mapped into MonoklError::Git { operation: "show", message } at its sole call site, git_scope::blob_at_ref (03-multi-language-platform.md:1537-1544). This exception is closed as of this draft — confirmed via grep across both named Parts to be the only bare-error-type helper matching this shape. main()/run() (-> miette::Result<()>, 01-core-architecture.md:2448-2515) and the napi FFI boundary (-> napi::Result<T>, 01-core-architecture.md:2900-2922) are excluded from the quantifier's range by construction: both are documented conversion boundaries that consume an already-produced MonoklError rather than constructing one.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Naming the exact quantifier scope (two specific documents, one named exception) rather than leaving 'the spec' undefined is a drafting judgment, verified twice against source via grep with no counterexample found beyond the one named exception.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Io(#[from] FileIoError) is #[error(transparent)] (01-core-architecture.md:200-201): its Display text is exactly whichever FileIoError variant it wraps produces — "failed to read {path}" (Read), "failed to write {path}" (Write), "failed to create directory {path}" (CreateDir), or "failed to remove {path}" (Remove), per io-errors/file_io.rs verbatim (01-core-architecture.md:2959-2984) — and its source() returns the wrapped io::Error via FileIoError's own #[source] field.

Walk { path: Utf8PathBuf, #[source] source: ignore::Error } has Display text exactly "walker error at {path}" (01-core-architecture.md:203-204). Three construction sites in the spec corpus, no more: text_search::search_files (01-core-architecture.md:1005-1008), WorkspaceIndex::build's walk (01-core-architecture.md:2206-2209), and source_scan's per-directory walk (03-multi-language-platform.md:2033). In all three, path is the root of the walk in progress, not the specific entry that failed.
RegexBuild(#[from] grep_regex::Error) has Display text exactly "regex compilation failed" (01-core-architecture.md:210-211).

NonUtf8Path { path: std::path::PathBuf } deliberately types path as std::path::PathBuf, not Utf8PathBuf — the entire point of the variant is that the path is not valid UTF-8, so it cannot be represented as camino's UTF-8-guaranteed type. Display text is exactly "non-UTF-8 path encountered: {path:?}" (01-core-architecture.md:213-214), Debug-formatted since std::path::Path/PathBuf do not implement Display.
TooManyTerms { count: usize, limit: usize } has Display text exactly "query has too many terms: {count} > {limit}" (01-core-architecture.md:216-217).

TokenizerInit is a unit variant (no fields) with Display text exactly "tokenizer init failed" (01-core-architecture.md:219-220), constructed at tiktoken_rs::o200k_base().map_err(|_| MonoklError::TokenizerInit)? (01-core-architecture.md:1240).

PathOutsideRoot { path: Utf8PathBuf } has Display text exactly "path outside workspace root: {path}" (01-core-architecture.md:225-226), fired by the dependents command when the canonicalized target file does not start with the canonicalized root argument (01-core-architecture.md:2332).

MonoklError::Json(#[from] serde_json::Error) (01-core-architecture.md:222-223) has exactly 8 raw, non-test call sites across the spec corpus where a serde_json operation is `?`-propagated (or explicitly .map_err(Into::into)) into a function returning crate::error::Result<_>, grouped into 3 logical categories, independently re-confirmed by two separate review rounds: cache-deserialize (1 site) — persist::load_cache's serde_json::from_str::<CacheFile>(&content)? (01-core-architecture.md:1602); cache-serialize (3 sites, all in persist.rs) — flush's serde_json::to_string_pretty(&cache)? (01-core-architecture.md:1665), evict_lru's in-loop recheck (line 1690), evict_lru's final fallback (line 1698); CLI/output-serialize (4 sites) — output::render_json (01-core-architecture.md:2409), output::render_json_compact (line 2416), projection::project_inspect_result (03-multi-language-platform.md:1594), projection::project_search_response (line 1602). Explicitly excluded: 02-inspection-and-analysis.md:1865's test helper run_ok_json, which uses .unwrap_or_else(...) (panics) and never touches MonoklError. This spec corrects the Json variant's Display text from "json serialization failed" to "json parsing or serialization failed" (a textual-accuracy fix to the existing literal at 01-core-architecture.md:222, not yet reflected in that file), since the cache-deserialize site (site 1) is a parse failure the old text mischaracterized as a serialization failure.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The 8-site count and 3-category grouping were independently re-derived from source (not just cited) in two separate review rounds with matching results — high confidence. The Display-text correction is a low-risk accuracy fix (an existing string is wrong about which direction of operation it describes), not a behavioral policy decision, so it stays in this track rather than being deferred with the corruption-policy question.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: InvalidGitRef { ref_: String, reason: &'static str } has Display text exactly "invalid git ref {ref_:?}: {reason}" (01-core-architecture.md:231-232). Exactly three reason literal values are constructed anywhere in the spec corpus, all in git_scope::validate_git_ref (03-multi-language-platform.md:1365-1385): "ref is empty" (empty input), "starts with '-' — refusing as it could be parsed as a git option" (git-option-injection guard), and "contains characters outside the safe set" (any char outside A-Za-z0-9_/.@{}^~:+-).

persist::load_cache(root, config_hash) (01-core-architecture.md:1586-1607) returns Err(MonoklError::StaleDiskCache) when cache.version != CACHE_VERSION || cache.config_hash != config_hash (line 1603-1604), where CACHE_VERSION is the constant defined in analysis/persist.rs (01-core-architecture.md:1513; currently 2) — this criterion binds to that constant symbolically, not to its literal value. load_cache() has exactly two callers in the spec corpus: persist::init(root, config_hash) (1567-1584) and persist::flush(root, config_hash)'s state.cache_file.is_none() fallback branch (1652-1658). init()'s match arm (1570-1581) intercepts Err(MonoklError::StaleDiskCache) only: logs a tracing::warn! (AC-020B) and substitutes a fresh empty CacheFile, never returning StaleDiskCache to init()'s own caller. Every other Err(e) from load_cache() — including MonoklError::Json and MonoklError::Io — propagates via init()'s Err(e) => return Err(e) arm (1580) unmodified. This spec does not change that match arm; it documents it as-is.

persist::flush(root, config_hash) (01-core-architecture.md:1652-1680), when state.cache_file is None at call time, calls load_cache(root, config_hash)? directly (line 1657) with no match arm and no interception of any kind — unlike init()'s handling (AC-013). Any Err from that call, including Err(MonoklError::StaleDiskCache) or Err(MonoklError::Json(_)), propagates unmodified via `?` straight to flush()'s own caller. In every call chain shown in this spec corpus, flush's sole caller (WorkspaceIndex::build, 01-core-architecture.md:2195-2258) calls persist::init(root, config_hash)? as its first statement (line 2201) before ever reaching flush() at the end of the same function (line 2256) — so in the documented call graph, state.cache_file is already Some by the time flush() runs, and this fallback branch is not exercised today. flush is pub(crate) (line 1652), not gated behind init at the type level, so nothing in the source prevents a future in-crate caller from invoking it before init(). This asymmetry is documented here, not resolved — fixing it means editing persist.rs's verbatim flush() body, out of scope (non_goals).
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Documenting a real, current gap without silently fixing code outside this track's editing authority is a scope judgment, independently verified twice: WorkspaceIndex::build's call order was re-confirmed in both review rounds.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Git { operation: &'static str, message: String } has Display text exactly "git {operation} failed: {message}" (01-core-architecture.md:234-235).

Exactly 2 of git_scope.rs's MonoklError::Git construction sites spell out a literal operation value in the spec corpus: (1) effective_pr_range's merge_base call — operation: "merge-base" (03-multi-language-platform.md:1395-1397); (2) blob_at_ref — operation: "show" (03-multi-language-platform.md:1540-1543). collect_changes (03-multi-language-platform.md:1419-1472) contains 3 additional fallible-git-operation sites whose map_err closures are elided (/* … */) in the source as shown, at lines 1428, 1430, and 1470 — their operation literals, and for 2 of the 3, even whether the constructed variant is MonoklError::Git at all, are undetermined by this document. This spec deliberately does not invent literal values for these 3 sites (non_goals) rather than assert a fact no document in this corpus states.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Choosing not to invent unfounded literals, and instead scoping AC-015 to only the 2 spelled-out sites, was independently re-verified against source in two review rounds with matching results (3 elisions, same line numbers both times).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: SymlinkRejected { path: Utf8PathBuf } has Display text exactly "refusing to read symlink: {path}" (01-core-architecture.md:237-238). Sole construction site: io_safety::read_to_string_capped (03-multi-language-platform.md:2113-2115), fired when symlink_metadata(path).file_type().is_symlink() is true, checked before the size check (AC-017). read_to_string_capped (03-multi-language-platform.md:2109) has no call site anywhere in this spec corpus, despite 03-multi-language-platform.md:2131's prose claiming it guards search/inspect/extract/refs/definition — that claim is refuted by docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 3 findings #2 and #16, which show extract and the refs/definition path use raw fs::read_to_string instead. SymlinkRejected is therefore currently unconstructible via any shown command path; wiring read_to_string_capped into those entry points is io_safety.rs implementation work, out of scope for this error-contract track (see non_goals).
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The 'used at user-facing entry points' claim in 03-multi-language-platform.md's own prose is contradicted by that same document's independently-verified edge-case audit (findings #2, #16) — reporting the refutation rather than the refuted prose is a drafting judgment, not a new design decision, so it stays in this track as a documentation-accuracy fix.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: FileTooLarge { path: Utf8PathBuf, size: u64, cap: u64 } has Display text exactly "file too large: {path} is {size} bytes, cap is {cap}" (01-core-architecture.md:240-241). Sole construction site: io_safety::read_to_string_capped (03-multi-language-platform.md:2117-2122), fired when meta.len() > MAX_INSPECTABLE_FILE_SIZE, where MAX_INSPECTABLE_FILE_SIZE = 50 * 1024 * 1024 = 52,428,800 bytes (03-multi-language-platform.md:2107). Like SymlinkRejected (AC-016), this variant shares read_to_string_capped's total unreachability in the current corpus — FileTooLarge is equally unconstructible via any shown command path today.

LockPoisoned { context: &'static str } has Display text exactly "internal lock poisoned in {context} — a prior panic left shared state possibly inconsistent; this is a bug, please report" (01-core-architecture.md:243-245). It is deliberately NOT auto-recovered via PoisonError::into_inner() — per the comment at 01-core-architecture.md:1556-1559, recovering would launder possibly-torn shared state back into use. Two confirmed construction sites: analysis::persist::lock_state() (01-core-architecture.md:1560, context: "analysis::persist::CacheState") and pipeline::session::WorkspaceSession::standard_index (03-multi-language-platform.md:1246-1248, context: "pipeline::session::WorkspaceSession::standard_index").
The crate-wide alias pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, MonoklError>; is defined in error.rs (01-core-architecture.md:248), immediately after the enum definition.

StaleDiskCache's own #[error(...)] Display literal (01-core-architecture.md:228) is corrected from "disk cache is stale (version or config mismatch); run `mnkl init --rebuild`" to exactly "disk cache is stale (version or config hash mismatch)" (a textual-accuracy fix to the existing literal, not yet reflected in that file). The remediation clause naming `mnkl init --rebuild` is removed outright, not reworded: the corpus contains three successive Subcmd enums — cli.rs's original 5-variant enum (01-core-architecture.md §21), an intermediate 16-variant revision explicitly labeled "The complete Subcmd enum from cli.rs" (02-inspection-and-analysis.md:54-58, adding Inspect/Patterns/Tokens/Definition/Refs/Diff/Explain/Coverage/DataFlow/Similar/plus one more over the original 5), and the final 20-variant superseding enum (03-multi-language-platform.md:2212-2342, adding Deps/DepsFrom/Classify/MigrationSurface/Schema over the 16) — no init subcommand exists in any of the three. No recovery-action language is added in its place, since per AC-013B this message can reach a caller in an un-recovered state via flush's fallback, and a recovery claim would not always be true.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Removing a reference to a nonexistent CLI command is a low-risk accuracy fix (07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 finding #6), independently re-confirmed in two review rounds as a real defect in the source. It is not deferred alongside the corruption-policy question because it changes no behavior — only a misleading string.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The tracing::warn! log line at persist::init's StaleDiskCache-interception arm (01-core-architecture.md:1573) is a criterion distinct from AC-020's enum Display literal: it is a plain log message emitted alongside the self-heal, never returned to any caller. Its exact, binding text, unchanged by this spec: "on-disk cache is stale (version or config_hash mismatch); starting fresh".

Within the scope of variants and call sites this spec resolves, MonoklError's default posture is propagate-to-caller via `?` (or an explicit map_err/Into::into at the construction boundary, for the AC-003 exception). The sole documented exception is StaleDiskCache, and only when load_cache is reached via persist::init specifically — not via persist::flush's fallback, where the identical variant propagates uncaught (AC-013B). This spec does not claim to resolve, and explicitly defers (non_goals), the cache.json corruption-vs-staleness recovery policy, the regex-term call-site inconsistency (07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md Part 1 finding #7), and the NonUtf8Path call-site inconsistency (Part 1 finding #12) — those remain real, separately-tracked exceptions to a clean propagate-vs-intercept split, outside this spec's scope.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Rewritten after canon-auditor's second-round finding that an earlier version of this criterion overclaimed a corpus-wide 'sole exception' when other real (if out-of-scope) exceptions exist elsewhere in the corpus. This version scopes the claim explicitly to what this spec resolves, and names the deferred exceptions instead of silently omitting them.

linked_research: docs/spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md (Part 1 findings #5 [corrupted cache.json, deferred not resolved — see non_goals], #6 [StaleDiskCache's nonexistent-command message, resolved AC-020], #19 [render_error-vs-miette, non_goal]) and docs/architecture/error-taxonomy.md (Known contract gaps 1 and 2).
revision_note: Second correction pass, plus a final narrow patch after a fourth gate attempt. Round 1 (canon-drafter's first correction) fixed citation hygiene and grounding but introduced a new problem: it resolved the cache.json corruption-vs-staleness recovery policy (a genuine new design decision) via judgment_call criteria that two independent review rounds could not get to hold up — round 2's canon-verifier found the claimed Json-interception code doesn't exist anywhere in the verbatim source, and canon-auditor found the same thing plus a structural diagnosis: bundling a new design decision into a faithful-correction spec violates this project's own CLAUDE.md process (new design questions require a superpowers:brainstorming pass first). This draft acted on that diagnosis directly rather than attempting a third patch: AC-021 (self-heal Json) and AC-022 (distinguishable warn! text) were removed entirely; AC-013/AC-013B now describe only the current, real, unresolved behavior (StaleDiskCache-only interception at init, no interception at flush's fallback) without asserting a fix that isn't backed by any shown code; the corruption-policy question is named explicitly in non_goals as deferred to a follow-on track gated on brainstorming; the final criterion (AC-021) was rewritten to scope its 'default posture' claim to what this spec actually resolves, naming the other known exceptions instead of overclaiming past them. AC-011's Display-text correction and AC-020's mnkl-init-rebuild removal were kept in this track as low-risk textual-accuracy fixes, not new behavioral decisions. A subsequent gate attempt (retry_count 2) found two further narrow defects unrelated to the corruption-policy split — AC-005 undercounted Walk's construction sites (1 of 3 named) and AC-016 asserted a reachability for SymlinkRejected/FileTooLarge that the corpus's own edge-case audit (Part 3 findings #2, #16) refutes (read_to_string_capped has zero call sites anywhere) — both patched directly (AC-005 now lists all three sites; AC-016/AC-017 state the unreachability with citations; a matching non_goal was added). Gate attempt 4 (retry_count 3) passed with zero blockers and three non-blocking notes, addressed in this same pass: AC-020's Subcmd citation updated to also reference the superseding 20-variant enum, and docs/architecture/error-taxonomy.md's line-63 restatement of the now-refuted read_to_string_capped reachability claim corrected to match.
reasoning: This is a subtractive correction built directly on facts both prior review rounds independently verified twice over (the 8-site Json enumeration, the 2-caller/1-interception load_cache structure, the 3 elided Git operation tags, LockPoisoned's 2 sites, the blob_at_ref_in_repo exception) — none of that grounding work needed to be redone, only the corruption-policy material needed to be removed and the dependent criteria (AC-013, AC-013B, AC-023) rewritten to stop asserting facts that removal invalidates. The one genuinely new judgment made in this pass is procedural, not factual: recognizing that canon-auditor's second-round finding wasn't 'fix this criterion's wording' but 'this criterion shouldn't be in this spec at all,' and acting on that rather than attempting a third wording patch on a decision that was never this track's to make unilaterally.
